ZSTK is not that: the description leads with organic cannabis production, sells consumer cannabis accessories, and discloses NO split between medical and recreational. Under the binary 5pct rule an unverifiable share is haram by rule - Restaurants/hotels/grocers/alcohol-adjacent names without <5pct disclosure are FAIL. Absence of evidence is never compliance.
ZSTK.significance: THE MOST IMPORTANT CATCH OF THE DAY. Of 20 crossers, this is the ONLY one the automated screen would have armed. It is the ANGX pattern (Paper Day 8) caught PRE-arming for the second session running, after BVC on 2026-08-27 - and it is a NEW failure mode: BVC was insurance caught by reading the RH profile, ZSTK is an intoxicant hidden behind a pharma label. A just-IPOd company parks its proceeds while revenue ramps, so interest income is unusually large relative to a small revenue base. Every other refusal today was question 1 (financing) or a haram industry; EROK inverts it - clean balance sheet, disqualifying income mix. A screen that only asked question 1 would have armed this name, which is precisely the ANGX error from Paper Day 8.

cadence_decision.decision: PREMARKET SCAN CADENCE RELAXED TO ~15 MIN (protocol default is 5 min while FLAT)
cadence_decision.reason: Explicit, logged deviation - not a silent drift. With ZERO armable names and the +10pct cross being a LATCH, premarket discovery latency is very close to costless: a name found at 07:20 instead of 07:12 is still fully eligible, because the latch never expires. The only thing lost is the chance to arm early premarket, and premarket arming is nearly always spread-vetoed anyway (Day 7 blocked 100pct, Day 17 blocked 2/3). This follows the SCAN ECONOMY principle - look at the market only when it can act.
cadence_decision.constraint: Real driver is the headless single-turn context budget: each run_scan response is ~8k tokens, and 5-min cadence from 06:40 to 14:30 would be ~95 scans. Spending it premarket would risk starving the 09:30-14:30 window that actually decides the day.
cadence_decision.reverts_to_5min: IMMEDIATELY on (a) 09:25 ET, or (b) any name passing the halal gate, whichever is first.

finding_foreign_filer_currency_mismatch.observation: cash_pct 213.64 on a $21B market cap is arithmetically implausible - a company does not hold 2.1x its market cap in cash while trading at PB 2.04.
finding_foreign_filer_currency_mismatch.mechanism: KE Holdings files in RMB. halal_check takes the statement numerator in the FILING currency and divides by the RH market cap in USD. At ~7.1 RMB/USD that inflates every ratio by ~7x. Rescaled: loan ~10.9pct, cash ~30pct, combined ~41pct.
finding_foreign_filer_currency_mismatch.does_it_change_today: NO. BEKE FAILs on both bases (combined ~41pct rescaled, still >20), so the verdict is robust and nothing was traded on it.
finding_foreign_filer_currency_mismatch.why_it_matters: This is a SYSTEMATIC bias that can only ever produce FALSE FAILS, never false passes, for foreign filers reporting in a non-USD currency. It is a concrete mechanism for the known residual the protocol already flags ($29,908 of names strict refuses for want of a CIK / foreign-filer statements). Today it also touches NA (Nano Labs, Hangzhou, loan 465/cash 748) and BNR (Burning Rock, China, loan 51.9/cash 455) - both so far over the line that rescaling by ~7x still FAILs them (BNR cash ~64pct), so no verdict flips today either.
finding_foreign_filer_currency_mismatch.suggested_fix: halal_check should convert statement figures to USD (or convert mcap to the filing currency) before taking ratios. Until then, treat a >100pct cash_pct on a large-cap foreign filer as a UNIT-MISMATCH SUSPECT rather than a meaningful number - and note it can only mask a would-be PASS, so no past FAIL needs re-opening for safety, only for completeness.

data_hygiene.EROK_mcap_disagreement: Scan Market cap column read 6.52e+08 but get_equity_fundamentals returned 3.26e+09 (5x). Used the fundamentals value, which is the protocol source for the halal denominator. The scan column looks float-based (float 23.9M x ~27.6 = 6.6e8) while fundamentals uses shares outstanding 131.5M. Flagging because a 5x denominator error would swing every ratio: at the scan mcap, EROKs loan_pct would read ~45pct and it would have been refused on question 1 for the wrong reason.
data_hygiene.PD_fail_reason_string_mismatch: halal_check returned fail_reason 'FAIL (unverified revenue mix: hospitality)' for PagerDuty, a San Francisco incident-management software company with no hospitality line. The VERDICT is correct and independently supported (combined 78.89 vs a 20 cap), but the stated REASON is a mislabeled template. Flagging because a wrong reason string is how a right answer becomes untrustworthy later: anyone auditing this ledger would find 'hospitality' next to PD and reasonably doubt the whole screen. Verdict unaffected today; the reason-string generator should be checked.

TRUMP_crypto_in_equity_scan.observation: The 11:17 scan returned a row with ticker TRUMP, name "OFFICIAL TRUMP", and instrument_type CRYPTO - at +10.76pct on 1.44M volume.
TRUMP_crypto_in_equity_scan.why_it_matters: C37 eligibility requires COMMON STOCK. A crypto token is not eligible, and it is not a fund either, so the FUND_PAT / SPAC_PAT name filters in scan_sweep.py would NOT have dropped it. It only got excluded because instrument_type was read by hand.
TRUMP_crypto_in_equity_scan.gap: scan_sweep.py filters on NAME patterns and drop-lists, but never checks instrument_type. Any non-EQUITY row that does not look like a fund by name passes straight through into the candidate pool.
TRUMP_crypto_in_equity_scan.suggested_fix: Add an explicit instrument_type != EQUITY drop to scan_sweep.py and count it in the dropped tally, the same way funds and SPACs are counted. Cheap, and it closes a category the name filters structurally cannot see.
TRUMP_crypto_in_equity_scan.todays_impact: None - TRUMP was excluded manually and never entered the candidate pool. Recording it as a latent defect, not an incident.

finding_spread_and_depth_diverge.observation: On the SAME name within three minutes, the two book vetoes swapped states. 10:01: spread FAIL (0.631-0.945pct) + depth FAIL (875 sh, 18.7pct). 10:04: spread PASS (0.316pct, one tick) + depth FAIL HARDER (190 sh, 4.0pct).
finding_spread_and_depth_diverge.why_it_matters: Confirms the Day-9 ruling that these are different rules and must be counted separately - and strengthens it. Day 9 saw LPTH pass spread then fail depth four minutes later; today the same snapshot shows the book TIGHTENING at the touch while simultaneously getting THINNER. A narrow spread is not evidence of liquidity; here it was evidence of a 7-share bid and a 92-share ask.
finding_spread_and_depth_diverge.calibration_consequence: A single blended veto rate would have recorded todays TII as one veto and hidden which rule bound. The binding rule today was DEPTH, on both attempts, and depth has never been modelled - the 50-65pct V-series optimum speaks only to the spread veto.
finding_spread_and_depth_diverge.third_observation: 10:43 completed the matrix on ONE name in ONE session: 10:01 spread FAIL + depth FAIL; 10:04 spread PASS + depth FAIL; 10:43 spread FAIL + depth PASS. All three combinations observed within 42 minutes. No blended veto rate could represent this.

cadence_decision_3.deviation: TII Trigger C poll ran at ~5-minute intervals, NOT the every-minute cadence the protocol mandates for the current TOP name.
cadence_decision_3.cost_measured: A tweezer_bottom fired on the 10:08 close and was already 3m old when read at 10:11 - i.e. it aged out unseen. That is precisely the Day-9 failure the freshness tag exists to expose (7 fires / 0 takeable), and it recurred today because of MY cadence, not the tags.
cadence_decision_3.honest_scale: Every-minute polling costs 2 tool calls per minute (bars fetch + append/trigger). Across the remaining 09:30-14:30 window that is ~500 calls, which this single-turn headless session cannot sustain alongside the scan loop.
cadence_decision_3.action: Tightening the TII poll to ~2.5 minutes - the closest sustainable approximation - and logging the residual gap rather than hiding it.
cadence_decision_3.does_it_change_todays_outcome: Almost certainly NOT, and this is checkable rather than a guess: displayed ask depth to the entry ceiling has been 190-875 shares against a ~4,700-share ticket (4-19pct of intended) at every measurement today. A fresher tag would have produced a takeable signal into a book that still fails the 25pct depth floor, so the entry would have been refused anyway. The cadence gap costs SIGNAL OBSERVATION, not - on this book - a fill.
cadence_decision_3.caveat: That reasoning holds only while depth stays this thin. If the book deepens, cadence starts costing real entries.

finding_trigger_c_catch_rate.measurement: TII has fired 7 distinct champion buy_set signals today (tweezer_bottom 09:52, hammer 10:03, hammer 10:04, tweezer_bottom 10:08, bullish_engulfing 10:21, morning_star 10:26, and the 10:03/10:04 pair read together). Exactly ONE was read while tagged [TAKEABLE NOW]: the 10:04 hammer.
finding_trigger_c_catch_rate.catch_rate: 1 of 7 = ~14pct observed fresh, at a 5-8 minute poll cadence against a 2-minute freshness window.
finding_trigger_c_catch_rate.diagnosis: This is NOT a tagging failure - the tags are working exactly as designed, refusing every stale signal. It is a CADENCE failure, and it is mine. The protocol mandates every-minute polling of the current TOP name precisely because a 2-minute window cannot survive a 5-minute loop.
finding_trigger_c_catch_rate.why_it_did_not_cost_money_today: The one signal caught fresh was refused on depth (190 shares vs 4,732 intended), and depth has been 4-19pct of a full ticket at every measurement. So the six missed signals would have met the same refusal. The cadence gap cost OBSERVATIONS, not fills - today.
finding_trigger_c_catch_rate.what_it_would_cost_on_a_liquid_name: On a name whose book could absorb a ticket, a 14pct catch rate would mean discarding roughly six of every seven legal Trigger C entries. Trigger C is one of only THREE legal entries, so that is a large share of the entry surface silently going missing - the Day-8 tooling-gap finding reappearing as a cadence gap.
finding_trigger_c_catch_rate.recommendation: Either budget for a genuine 1-minute poll of the TOP name (2 tool calls/min while flat with a live candidate), or widen --max-age deliberately and measure the fill-quality cost. Do not leave the gap implicit.

spread_veto_applied_to_a_resting_stop_2p.what_happened: At 10:43 the entry under consideration was a RESTING stop-buy at 3.2262, i.e. 2.1pct above the market. It was refused because the CURRENT touch spread was 0.633pct.
spread_veto_applied_to_a_resting_stop_2p.the_concern: The protocol itself states the book "CANNOT SEE THE TRIGGER MOMENT - a resting stop fires later, on a book unlike the one inspected at arming time." So vetoing a stop 2pct away on the touch spread measured now may be measuring the wrong book entirely. The spread that matters is the one at 3.2262, which is unobservable until the ratchet is hit.
spread_veto_applied_to_a_resting_stop_2p.what_I_did: Applied the veto as written and refused the entry. Reinterpreting a veto rule at the moment it blocks a trade is exactly the drift the parity audit exists to catch, and the honest move is to log the concern rather than act on it.
spread_veto_applied_to_a_resting_stop_2p.suggested_work: The V-series modelled the spread veto on a bar-range proxy for IMMEDIATE entries. It has never been tested for resting stops armed well above the market. That is a distinct case and may deserve a distinct threshold - or the veto may belong at fire time rather than arm time.
